title: Phase Transition of Interactive Fixed-Effects Coefficients under Heterogeneous Spiked Factors
banked_reason: Even after repairing the proof and citation gaps, the exact-oracle sensitivity result remains below field level because it has four hand-crafted finite-array orthogonalities, no robustness to approximate or estimable residualization, and no applied evidence.

proof_attempt_summary: The run reduced the absorption problem to an explicit 2-by-2 spiked-SVD profile, derived a singleton global-profile characterization and an exact phase threshold, and verified the primary rectangular-Gaussian outlier citation. It stopped at D0.5 because the field-level promise remained an exact-oracle sensitivity result, while global stochastic localization, masked-factor rates, the all-subcritical fixed-rank citation, and the advertised negative inference witness were still unresolved. The only credible novelty lift requires a new approximate or estimable orthogonality model class, so it is outside this run's scope.
tldr: This paper studies an abstract exact-oracle panel experiment in which four finite-array orthogonality restrictions remove ordinary baseline confounding without fixing the profiled coefficient.  The full-sample IFE coefficient has a uniformly localized two-by-two spiked-SVD profile with an always-separated singleton minimizer.  It equals the ATT coordinate exactly when \(|h|\le h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\), and beyond that threshold it moves strictly toward the common effect.  The absorbed phase is relatively open and is nonempty exactly when \(\overline h>\min_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\); on its compact subsets the conventional residualized IFE Wald interval has asymptotically zero coverage.  Masked fitting remains an internal benchmark control.
gap: Existing panel theory covers regular strong factors, generic weak-factor robustness, or the strong bad-control endpoint, while random-matrix theory fixes the spike before taking limits. None controls a bounded coefficient-indexed treatment spike in the global IFE criterion after ordinary baseline-confounding terms have been removed by defining restrictions.
fill: The project derives \(\Phi_{\eta,h}\), proves bounded-local profile convergence and the absorption map on stable-singleton geometries, isolates tie selection as an open question, derives conventional-Wald failure, and uses masked fitting only as an internal control within the same abstract experiment.
